"""Paired family-bootstrap comparison of one run configuration against another on the same targets.
For each (split, n, method) present in both target-level tables: per benchmark the RMSE ratio to uniform|mean in each table (each table's own
uniform|mean), the family resample is shared by both tables, and the statistic is the geometric mean over non-thin benchmarks of
ratio_B / ratio_A.  A value < 1 means table B is more accurate.  (Both tables must hold the same targets: same split, same folds.)
usage: python3 -I scripts/09_paired.py TL_A.parquet TL_B.parquet OUT.csv [--split extrap] [--n 100] [--targets TARGETS.csv]"""
import os
for v in ("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[v] = "1"
import sys, argparse
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("a"); ap.add_argument("b"); ap.add_argument("out")
ap.add_argument("--split", default="extrap"); ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=100)
ap.add_argument("--targets", default="results/targets.csv")
ap.add_argument("--base", default="uniform|mean")
args = ap.parse_args()
B = 2000
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
tg = pd.read_csv(args.targets).set_index(["bench", "split"])
cols = ["bench", "split", "n", "method", "family", "target_model", "fold", "sq_err", "n_draws"]
T = [pd.read_parquet(p, filters=[("split", "==", args.split), ("n", "==", args.n)], columns=cols) for p in (args.a, args.b)]
methods = sorted(set(T[0].method) & set(T[1].method))
benches = sorted(b for b in set(T[0].bench) & set(T[1].bench) if not tg.loc[(b, args.split), "thin"])
rows = []; logs = {m: [] for m in methods}; pts = {m: [] for m in methods}; draws = {m: [] for m in methods}
for b in benches:
    g = [t[t.bench == b] for t in T]
    key = g[0][g[0].method == args.base][["fold", "target_model", "family"]].sort_values(["fold", "target_model"])
    ufam = np.unique(key.family); F = len(ufam)
    C = rng.multinomial(F, np.ones(F) / F, size=B).astype(float)
    cnt = np.bincount(np.searchsorted(ufam, key.family), minlength=F).astype(float); den = C @ cnt
    rm = []
    for t in g:
        d = {}
        for m, h in t.groupby("method"):
            h = h.sort_values(["fold", "target_model"])
            assert (h.target_model.values == key.target_model.values).all(), (b, m)
            se = np.bincount(np.searchsorted(ufam, h.family), h.sq_err.values.astype(float), F)
            d[m] = (np.sqrt((C @ se) / den), np.sqrt(se.sum() / cnt.sum()), h.n_draws.iloc[0])
        rm.append(d)

        pts[m].append((np.log(rm[0][m][1] / rm[0][args.base][1]), np.log(rm[1][m][1] / rm[1][args.base][1])))
        draws[m].append((rm[0][m][2], rm[1][m][2]))
for m in methods:
    A = np.stack([x[0] for x in logs[m]]); Bm = np.stack([x[1] for x in logs[m]])

analysis → story, inner50 paired interval: done, in `results/inner50/paired_vs_main.csv` (script `scripts/09_paired.py`, pushed to main).

Setting: extrap, n = 100, 13 non-thin benchmarks, same targets and same sampled designs in both runs. For each benchmark the ratio of RMSE to `uniform|mean` is computed in each run, the family resample is shared, and the statistic is the geometric mean over benchmarks of ratio(inner share 0.5) / ratio(main inner split).

| method | main | inner 0.5 | paired ratio [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| balanced × diff-irt | 0.815 | 0.763 | 0.936 [0.924, 0.952] |
| balanced × diff-knn | 0.846 | 0.802 | 0.948 [0.931, 0.971] |
| balanced × diff-ridge | 0.819 | 0.896 | **1.094 [1.077, 1.113]** |
| pps × diff-irt | 0.850 | 0.808 | 0.950 [0.935, 0.966] |
| strat × diff-irt | 0.865 | 0.853 | 0.986 [0.978, 0.999] |
| uniform × diff-irt | 0.854 | 0.809 | 0.947 [0.939, 0.961] |

So the move for balanced × diff-irt is a 6.4% RMSE reduction and it is precise (the paired interval is about ±1.4%, much narrower than the separate ones). Two cautions for the text: (1) the effect is not uniform — the ridge difference estimator gets 9% worse with the larger inner share, so "more held-out inner data helps the λ choice" holds for the IRT and kNN predictors, not for ridge; (2) the intervals are over families only (the sampled designs are identical across the two runs, so Monte-Carlo noise in the design draws is shared, not averaged out), and inner50 was chosen after seeing the main result, so it stays a post-hoc diagnostic, not a new headline. Estimators whose fit does not use the inner split (mean, model, plugin, calreg, fixed λ) give exactly 1.000, a check that the pairing is right.

shown.message:
I added the paired interval for the larger-gap inner split and posted it on story-repo's request in `experiment-repo`#5. The recalibrated-estimator (`extra`) and 100-draw (`highR`) jobs are still queued or running, so those results aren't in yet.

For balanced × difference-IRT on extrap at n=100, the RMSE ratio to uniform falls from 0.815 to 0.763. The paired change is a ratio of 0.936 [0.924, 0.952] over 13 non-thin benchmarks.

The effect is not uniform. The ridge difference estimator gets worse with the larger inner share, at 1.094 [1.077, 1.113]. Both inner-split variants share the same sampled designs, so the interval covers family resampling only.

The numbers are in `results/inner50/paired_vs_main.csv`, produced by the new `scripts/09_paired.py`. I also added it to `scripts/run_all.sh` and `RESULTS_SCHEMA.md` and pushed to `experiment-repo` main (a464a38). It has not yet been copied to `code/` in paper-repo `dev`. I'll do that with the `extra`/`highR` delivery.

When those jobs finish I'll analyse them and reply on idea-repo#6, story-repo#5 and paper-repo#7. I'll also fill in the CPU-hours in `REPRODUCE.md`, re-deliver `code/` and name the new files for paper-repo and figtab-repo.
